text:
mira: heads-up — noticed ~40% token/sec drop on canary after yesterday's runtime merge (sha 9f3a2b). CI perf alert fired this morning :grimacing:
deploy-bot: canary rollout completed: runtime-v2.14 -> 3 nodes in us-west2 at 02:13 UTC
ci-bot: perf-regression: throughput drop detected on integration perf suite (p95 tok/sec), test: runtime/throughput-1000. See: https://ci.internal/perf/3350012345
jonathan: link to grafana? trying to correlate with scheduling metrics
alejandra: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/p/rt/throughput?orgId=1&from=now-6h&to=now — big dip aligned with the rollout window. attaching a quick flame output
alejandra: ```
# simplified flame (top 3):
choose_kernel (kernel_select.cpp)          60.2%
continuous_batcher::drain (ctb.cpp)       24.8%
kv_cache::lookup (kvcache.cpp)            8.7%
```
sam_t: kv hitrate also fell from 89% -> 55% for the same workload around the dip. suspecting KV warmup + different kernel path amplifies small-batch overhead
perf-bot: recent PRs in the deploy range: r/infra/runtime#482 (scheduler: batch-splay heuristic), r/serving#491 (kernel policy: prefer small-copy kernel for short sequences), r/runtime#499 (ctb: drain backoff tweak)
ryan: can we get a trace from a single affected request? need to see kernel selection runtime and memcpy counts
mira: captured an async trace (stack + kernel tag) for a slow request, attaching snippet: ```
TRACE: request=0x7f8a
  enqueue -> prefetch -> choose_kernel(small_copy) -> memcpy(2x) -> kernel_exec(small_copy) -> postcopy -> kv_miss -> fallback_kernel
  total_tokens=256, latency=420ms
```
jonathan: small_copy kernel has higher per-token cost once it hits memcpy fallback for >128 tokens. If scheduler is splitting into many small batches, we force that path more often
alejandra: the batcher metrics show median batch size dropped from 18 -> 6 in the canary nodes starting at 02:12. queue_wait_time increased too (median +90ms)
mira: hypothesis: batch-splay heuristic change in r/infra/runtime#482 made the admission prefer earlier dispatch for older requests which reduced coalescing and promoted small_copy kernel selection. combo with ctb drain tweak in r/runtime#499 -> token/sec collapse
jonathan: running quick local bisect on commit range: start=origin/main@9f3a2b end=origin/main@prev-release. Will run `git bisect run ./bench/local_throughput.sh` and report
mira: in the meantime hold rollout? I can pause further canary promotions and pin canary to previous runtime
deploy-bot: action: rollout paused on canary (manual hold) by mira at 06:45 UTC :warning:
sam_t: +1 hold. I'll collect kv memstats and confirm whether kvcache eviction pattern changed after the scheduler tweak
alejandra: assigning deeper profiling to myself. plan: perf trace across kernel_select path, record memcpy counts, and run microbench for small_copy vs large_copy kernels. tagging @eng-runtime :eyes:
jonathan: preliminary bisect result looks like the batch-splay heuristic change is the likely culprit. local perf run shows throughput drop reintroduces when that commit is present
perf-bot: CI perf artifact: https://ci.internal/artifacts/3350012345/flame-ctb.tar.gz (contains perf traces and batch histograms)
ryan: next steps: (1) revert batch-splay heuristic in a hotfix PR and run canary (2) if revert restores tok/sec, schedule follow-up to rework heuristic with guardrails, (3) add regression test in perf-suite for batch-size distribution and kernel selection flag coverage
mira: agreed. I'll open the hotfix PR to revert r/infra/runtime#482 and tag ops. jira: PERF-1287 created and assigned to jonathan + alejandra + sam_t
jonathan: ETA for revert + canary run ~ 90m. I'll post updates.
mira: thanks all. holding rollout, tracking in PERF-1287. if anyone finds conflicting evidence ping here
alejandra: quick note — the root cause seems to be a feedback loop: smaller batches -> small_copy kernel -> memcpy fallback -> longer runtimes -> scheduler sees older requests -> splay more -> even smaller batches. classic amplification
sam_t: capturing kv cache warmup plan: force-prefix-cache run on canary to restore hitrate faster while we test revert
jonathan: update: local canary with revert applied restores median batch size to ~17 and tok/sec back to expected. preparing PR now
mira: :thumbsup: good signal. leave this thread as the single source of truth for the rollback and follow-ups
